body.reasoning: The loss involves water from a burst supply line, which would fall under exclusion E-17, but E-17 does NOT apply when the discharge is "sudden and accidental" as defined in Clause 1(a) of the endorsement, and the hose failure meets that definition because it was an abrupt, unforeseen event discovered within a short period (the family was out for dinner only) [HO-0304_03-24#05][HO-0304_03-24#02]. Therefore the damage is covered under Coverage A up to policy limits, subject to the duty to retain the failed component for inspection [HO-0304_03-24#06].

summary:
CLAIM NUMBER: CLM-2024-20052  
DATE OF LOSS: 2024-08-14  
POLICY FORMS: HO-0509 ed. 06-24  
LOSS: Two work laptops, valued at $2,800 total, were taken to a client's office and stolen from the meeting room.  
COVERAGE POSITION: UNDETERMINED  
GROUNDS: HO-0509 Clause 1 Definition of Home business and Business property  
EXCESS: 250  
REASONING: Clause 1 defines “home business” and “business property” and limits coverage for business property away from the residence to $500 (Clause 2) [HO-0509_06-24#02][HO-0509_06-24#03]. The facts do not establish whether the insured meets the “home business” definition, so it is unclear if the laptops fall under the business property sublimit or under standard personal property coverage, which is not provided in the attached endorsement [HO-0509_06-24#02]. Without that determination, coverage cannot be concluded [HO-0509_06-24#03].  
NEXT STEP: Obtain documentation of the insured’s home‑business gross receipts for the prior 12 months to determine if the business‑property sublimit applies.

body.loss: Two work laptops, valued at $2,800 total, were taken to a client's office and stolen from the meeting room.

grounds: HO-0509 Clause 1 Definition of Home business and Business property
body.subject_to: Insured must meet the definition of a "home business" (gross receipts > $5,000 in the prior 12 months) for the laptops to be considered "business property" subject to the off‑premises sublimit.
body.reasoning: Clause 1 defines "home business" and "business property" and limits coverage for business property away from the residence to $500 (Clause 2) [HO-0509_06-24#02][HO-0509_06-24#03]. The facts do not establish whether the insured meets the "home business" definition, so it is unclear if the laptops fall under the business property sublimit or under standard personal property coverage, which is not provided in the attached endorsement [HO-0509_06-24#02]. Without that determination, coverage cannot be concluded.
body.missing: Whether the insured's home business generated gross receipts exceeding $5,000 in the 12 months before the loss.
